guide.title: Giveaway guide
guide.subtitle: The steps to get it running and what to do when something does not go as expected
guide.s1b: In {{create}} set the prize, the duration, how many winners there will be and how long they have to answer. In {{requirements}} and {{weights}} you choose who can take part and who has a higher chance. Save with the button at the top.
guide.s2t: Choose where people can take part
guide.s2b: In {{platforms}} you turn Twitch and Kick on. Kick only lets you check roles (subscriber, VIP, moderator): other requirements are skipped or rejected depending on what you pick there.
guide.s3b: With the button in {{create}} or by typing {{start}} in chat. People enter with the entry command you defined. In {{participants}} you see who entered, their weight, chance and status, and you can search for someone to know whether they are in.
guide.s4b: With {{choose}} or from the panel. In OBS the roulette appears and then the winners. Each winner has their time to write anything in chat; if they do not, the bot announces it in a single message when the time reaches 0.
guide.s5b: With automatic re-draw on, their place is covered on its own. Otherwise use {{reroll}} (replaces every expired winner) or {{rerollUser}} to re-draw one specific person. When you are done, use {{finish}}.
guide.s6b: {{overlay}} has the link for the browser source and a button to simulate a full draw without touching chat. Theme, text, animations and sound are adjusted in their own tabs.
guide.noteSettingsTitle: Changes apply to the next giveaway
guide.noteSettings: A giveaway that has already started keeps the settings it started with. If you change something, cancel it and start another.
guide.noteDebug: The ones the Debug tab generates never answer: they are useful to see the roulette and the notices, but their winners will always expire.
guide.noteCommandsTitle: Everything can be done from chat
guide.noteCommands: Start, draw, re-draw, pick by hand, close entries and finish each have a command. The full list is in {{commands}}.

weights.title: Weights and Multipliers
weights.subtitle: Raise the chances of certain users
weights.watchExample: Example: with 1.1×, someone who watched 3 hours has 1.331× the chance (1.1³)
weights.bitsHint: More bits donated = higher chance. Only bits the viewer donates while the giveaway is active count.
weights.infoBody: A 2.0x multiplier means the user has double the chance of winning. Multipliers stack (e.g. Sub Tier 3 + VIP = 6.0 × 1.5 = 9.0x). Time, bits and streak multipliers apply per hour, 100 bits or month: 1.1 means +10 % for each one, compounded (at 10 hours that is 1.1 to the power of 10 ≈ 2.6x). So nobody hogs the draw there are caps you can change in Settings → Weight limits. A value below 1 penalizes, and only has effect if you lower the «Minimum weight» in those same settings.

cmdWhat.start: Starts the saved giveaway. With a prize and a duration (90s, 10m, 2h) or «manual», those apply only to this giveaway. Alias: iniciar
cmdWhat.choose: Draws the winners of the free places (all of them, or just one in «one by one»). With «leave open» and every place filled, it adds an extra winner. With a user, that person wins. Aliases: elegir, end, fin, sortear, terminar
cmdWhat.reroll: Replaces EVERY winner whose time ran out (or the first pending one if none ran out), with a backup or at random. With @user of a winner, re-draws that person even if they answered; with @user who is not a winner, that user takes the first unanswered place. Alias: resortear
cmdWhat.pick: Picks by hand: that person takes a free place or replaces the winner who did not answer
cmdWhat.finish: Ends the giveaway, closes entries and announces how many winners answered. Aliases: finalizar, listo
cmdWhat.close: Closes entries: nobody else can enter. Alias: cerrar
cmdWhat.cancel: Cancels the running giveaway. Alias: cancelar
cmdWhat.status: Shows the status: prize, participants and time left. Alias: estado

look.easingHelp: How it decelerates. Quint is the closest to a real wheel.
look.revealSecondsHelp: How long the winner stays on screen. With "Only while spinning", the wheel leaves the scene after this time.
look.visibilityHelp_spin: Hidden while idle. It comes in when a spin arrives and leaves after showing the winner; with queued spins it stays until the last one.
look.visibilityHelp_always: The wheel is on screen all the time, spinning or not.
look.visibilityHelp_registration: The wheel appears when you open entries and grows with each entrant; it spins on the draw and leaves when entries close. Every new entrant shows a card with their name and the total.
look.celebrationHelp: What goes with the winner reveal.
look.soundsHelp: Touch nothing and Decatron's pack plays. You can mute any of them or use your own.
look.soundPlaceholder: Pick from your library or paste a URL
look.tickOnlyDefault: Decatron's or silence only: it plays dozens of times per spin and audio with a tail sounds awful repeated.
look.soundWhen_spin_tick: Every time the needle crosses a segment.
look.soundWhen_spin_slowdown: During the final stretch of the spin. It ends right as the wheel stops.
look.soundWhen_reveal: When it stops on the winning segment.
look.soundWhen_win_celebration: Along with the confetti, after the reveal.
look.soundWhen_raffle_draw: When the wheel starts drawing among the entrants.
look.soundWhen_raffle_winner: Along with the confetti, when the raffle winner comes out.
look.soundWhen_spin_tick_card: The drumroll while the card shakes, faster and faster until it flips.
look.typoHelp: The lettering on the segments and the winner card. The list is fixed on purpose: OBS doesn't have your computer's fonts installed, so a hand-typed font would look right here and come out as something else on stream.
look.fontHelp: Each option is shown in its own lettering.
look.fontWeightHelp: How heavy the segment lettering is.
look.fontOneWeight: This font ships with a single weight.
look.textScaleHelp: Scales every label at once. The wheel still shrinks them on its own for long labels and narrow segments, so they never spill out of the wedge.
look.textUppercaseHelp: Writes the labels in uppercase without retyping them.
look.textColorHelp: The text drawn on each segment.
look.textOutlineHelp: A border around the letters. Helps when the segments are light-coloured and the text gets lost.
look.presentationHelp: How the result gets drawn. The draw itself is the same in all of them: the server picks the winner and the presentation only animates up to it.
look.presentationRowHelp: Saved per wheel, not per channel: you can keep a big wheel for subs and a faster one for bits.
look.presentationOnlyOne: only the wheel for now; the strip, the reel and the grid plug in here
look.pointerHelpNeedle: The needle that marks the winning slice. Changing sides is not just cosmetic: the wheel stops offset so the needle keeps pointing at the right prize.
look.pointerHelpViewer: The frame around the winning cell. It is this presentation’s equivalent of the needle.
look.pointerHiddenHelp: The wheel still stops where it stops; the marker just is not drawn.
look.pointerSideHelp: Top is where everyone looks first, but you can move it if something in your scene covers that area.
look.pointerCapsHelp: The two tips are what make it read as a sight and not as a plain box.
look.pointerColorHelp: Follows the wheel accent color by default.
look.backgroundBoxNote: The background is painted around the wheel only, not across the whole screen. In the Canvas tab you can decide exactly which area it covers.
look.templatesHelp: A whole look in one click: colors, typography, pointer and celebration. They do not move anything around or change the draw format, and nothing is saved until you press Save.

media.title: Media library
media.help: Your usual library, filtered by the "wheel" category. Whatever you upload here can be picked in Look. Storage quota is your plan's, not a separate one for the wheel.

history.empty: No spins to show with these filters yet.

history.distHelp: The thick bar is the real frequency; the thin one below it, the probability you configured. Metrics use the whole history, not just what the table shows.
history.fewSpins: With few spins the two bars will differ quite a bit, and that's normal: chance takes a while to look like its own table.

wallets.title: Contribution wallets
wallets.help: Each viewer's credit balance. They belong to the channel, not to one wheel: whoever contributes once can spend on any of your wheels.
wallets.empty: Nobody has credits on this channel yet.
wallets.lifetimeNote: The balance is set, not added to: type the number you want it to end at. Lifetime never goes down, not even when a balance is corrected by hand.

rules.title: Draw rules
rules.help: They change which segment can come up. None of them touch the drawing: the wheel still shows every segment, whether it can come up or not.
rules.noRepeatHelp: Stops the same result coming up twice in a row. If the rule would leave a single possible segment, it's ignored: better a repeat than no spin.
rules.pityHelp: After several spins in a row with no prize, the next one can't be “nothing” again. Counted per viewer.
rules.multiHelp: Lets a viewer spend several spins at once. Each spin is its own draw: stock runs down between them.
rules.multiNote: In chat it's used like this: {{command}} 5. It's charged all at once or not at all, and the bot answers with a single summary message.

canvas.help: Place the wheel, the winner card and the watermark on a 1920x1080 screen. Drag to move, use the corners to resize.

canvas.fixedNote: This wheel uses fixed 1920x1080 positions. The OBS browser source has to be exactly that size, or the design will be off.
canvas.bgColorNote: The color is chosen in the Look tab.
canvas.noImageYet: Pick an image or a video

prizes.description: A wheel that spins on screen and hands out prizes to your community.
prizes.what: Each slice has a weight and a prize. Your viewers collect credits (with bits, subs, gifted subs, donations or channel points), pay for a spin and the bot decides the prize. The overlay only animates the result.
prizes.test: Press “Test spin” above to watch it spin in your overlay. In the Test tab you can simulate a contribution (bits, subs…) to see how many credits it would give.

raffle.description: A raffle where the slices are the people who joined.
raffle.what: People join with a command while entries are open. You or your moderators open and close them, and the bot picks the winner. The overlay only animates the draw.
raffle.test: Open entries from the Raffle tab, type the command in your chat to join, and draw from there or with “!drueda sortear”.

liveTranslation.title: Live translation
liveTranslation.subtitle: Your voice is transcribed, translated and dubbed in real time. Each viewer picks their language from the Decatron extension; only they hear it.
liveTranslation.notConfigured: The server has no voice services configured; the feature can't start yet.
liveTranslation.confirmStop: Stop the current session? The app will stop sending audio until you press Start again.

ext.title: 2 · Extension for your viewers

config.title: Settings
config.subtitle: Which languages you offer and which voice each one uses.
config.targetsHint: A language is only translated while someone is listening; no listeners, no voice credits spent.
config.voicesHint: One voice per language. With the standard voice you pick among the installed Piper voices.
config.announceHint: The bot tells chat the stream can be heard in other languages. Use {languages} for the list.
config.announcePlaceholder: 🌐 This stream can be heard in {languages} with the Decatron Translate extension: https://decatron.net/translate
config.backgroundHint: Suggested volume of your voice while the translation plays. Each viewer can change it.
config.engineHint: The standard voice runs on our server and costs no credits; it takes a bit longer to start speaking. Premium voices sound better and respond sooner, but charge credits per character. If you run out of credits mid-stream, the voice falls back to standard on its own and nothing stops.
config.recordHint: Leaves the original text, the translation and the timings of each phrase in the server log, to compare tests. Use it only for testing: the text of what you say stays in the log for up to 30 days. Off by default.

guide.title: Live translation: before you turn it on
guide.intro: Your viewers hear your stream in their language and the credits spent are yours. This guide explains what it costs and how to protect yourself.
guide.step1: Choose the language you speak, the target languages and each one's voice in
guide.step2: Review the limits: keep the recommended values or adjust them in
guide.step3: Open the desktop app and press Start. Your viewers choose their language in the Decatron extension; in Multi-view they see the subtitles.
guide.costIntro: The cost depends on the languages that are on, not on how many people listen:
guide.cost1: While the session is active you pay for recognizing your voice (per second), whether anyone listens or not.
guide.cost2: Each language with at least one listener turns on its own translation and synthesized voice, and that spends credits per character. A single listener is enough to turn a language on.
guide.cost3: The voice and translation of two languages cost about double those of one; twenty listeners in the same language cost the same as one.
guide.protectIntro: These limits always work, even with open access:
guide.protect1: Only a language you offer is accepted: asking for others turns nothing on.
guide.protect2: A single IP has a maximum of connections per channel and in total, so one browser opened many times cannot turn on all your languages.
guide.protect3: There is a maximum of join attempts per minute per IP.
guide.protect4: You choose the maximum number of listeners and of simultaneous languages; at the limit, joining is rejected with a notice.
guide.reco1: Simultaneous listeners: your plan's recommended value (leave it empty to use it).
guide.reco2: Simultaneous languages: 2, or 1 if you are just starting.
guide.reco4: If you notice anything odd, use the panic button in the Access tab.
guide.credits1: You cannot start a session without credits.
guide.credits2: If premium credits run out, the voice switches to the standard one (Piper) and the session continues.
guide.credits3: If they are not enough to recognize your voice, the session is cut and your viewers stop receiving the translation.
guide.panicBody: In the Access tab you can pause translation for your viewers: no one new gets in and those listening leave instantly. Your voice session stays active, so if you do not want to spend credits, stop the session too.
guide.protect5: You decide who can listen (everyone, signed in, followers, subscribers, VIPs, moderators or a list) and you can block people. The level is checked with your Twitch account and rechecked while they listen.
guide.reco5: Who listens: followers of 7 days or more. It needs a permission of your Twitch account; the Access tab tells you if it is missing.
guide.protect6: If someone probes your channel with dozens of attempts in a minute, the channel asks for sign-in for 30 minutes. What you saved does not change.
guide.protect7: In “Listening now” you see who is listening and can remove or block them.
guide.reco6: Credit cap per broadcast: multiply the hours you plan to speak by what an hour costs (the panel shows it) and add a 20% margin.
guide.credits4: Set a credit cap per broadcast so a long session never spends more than you decided: we warn you at 80% and it stops at 100%.
guide.credits5: If your balance lasts 15 minutes or less at the current pace, we warn you before it cuts out.
guide.example1: Who listens: followers of 7 days or more. Simultaneous languages: 2. Connections per IP: 3.
guide.example2: You speak about 3 hours per broadcast: if an hour costs about 200,000 credits, a cap of 720,000 covers the 3 hours with margin.
guide.example3: If one day you want to open it to everyone for an event, switch to “Everyone” and lower the listener cap; then go back to “Recommended”.

who.title: Who can listen

modeHint.everyone: Anyone, with or without an account. Only the limits below apply.
modeHint.logged_in: Anyone who has logged in to Decatron.
modeHint.followers: Followers of your Twitch channel (with a minimum time). Subscribers, VIPs and moderators also get in.
modeHint.subscribers: Subscribers of your channel (with a minimum tier). VIPs and moderators also get in.
modeHint.vip: Your VIPs. Moderators also get in.

who.noTwitch: You need a linked Twitch account to use this level.
who.unavailableSave: That level is not available: a permission of your Twitch account is missing. Authorize again and retry.
who.daysHint: Minimum number of days they have followed you. 0 = any follower.
who.tierHint: Subscribers of a lower tier do not get in.
who.allowHint: They get in even if they do not meet the level. One user per line.
who.blockHint: They never get in, even if they meet the level. One user per line.

budget.title: Credit cap per broadcast
budget.hint: If the session spends this total, translation stops by itself. We warn you at 80%. Leave it empty for no cap.
budget.cost: Based on your last {{sessions}} broadcasts, each hour of speech spends about {{perHour}} credits.
budget.noCost: There are not enough broadcasts yet to estimate what an hour costs.
budget.equals: That cap covers about {{hours}} h of speech.

abuse.body_flood: We saw {{attempts}} join attempts in one minute. For {{minutes}} min only signed-in people can join. Your saved settings did not change.

live.title: Listening now
live.hint: You can remove or block anyone. Signed-in people are blocked by account; anonymous ones by connection for one hour. The address is shown partly hidden.

live.error: The action could not be completed
